title: Human resources
description: Review how teams hire, onboard and plan staffing with defined responsibilities and limited access to personal data.
expertises: Privacy and human oversight in people processes
questions: Which role or team needs the change, and which hiring, onboarding or staffing outcome would improve?
Who conducts the process and who makes the final decision about an individual?
What information does each participant need, and where can the team use a blank template or aggregate count?

sources.title: U.S. Office of Personnel Management, Structured Interviews

specialists.title: Hiring process
specialists.focus: Check whether the role requirements can be observed through the same job-related questions and scoring rubric for each candidate.

specialists.title: Employee experience
specialists.focus: Identify what a new hire needs to do in their first weeks and assign each access, training and manager handoff to an owner.

specialists.title: Workforce planning
specialists.focus: Compare aggregate demand and available skills by team before recommending staffing, training or workload changes.

specialists.title: People data and oversight
specialists.focus: Check which steps need personal data, who can access it and when the responsible HR or privacy owner should intervene.

evidence: Review the approved job description, blank interview guide and scoring rubric for alignment with the work.
Inspect the onboarding checklist, access request flow and role-based permissions for missing handoffs or overlapping ownership.
Use authorized aggregate staffing, workload or time-to-completion data. Leave identifiable personnel records outside the consultation.
Check documented access, retention and escalation responsibilities with the authorized HR or privacy owner.
challenge: Question any criterion based on a vague notion of fit. Identify the work requirement and the evidence that would substantiate it.
Check whether the proposed process collects information that the next person in the workflow can do without.
When the team needs a legal interpretation or a decision about an identifiable person, refer it to the authorized human owner and keep the board focused on process design.
decision_criteria: Prefer a documented process with observable job requirements and the same assessment steps for candidates for the same role.
Name the human decision owner, the people who can access each data category and the point at which the record should be removed or reviewed.
Choose a way to measure the process with authorized aggregate data, such as whether new hires receive required access by the agreed date.
